problem: The text says 'The load has inertia J (kg·m²) and viscous friction b', which suggests J is only the external load. The equation J dω/dt + bω = T then only holds if J and b are the total inertia and damping referred to the motor shaft, including the rotor itself. A student may use only the load inertia and get a wrong answer.
fix: Say: 'J is the total inertia (rotor plus load referred to the shaft) in kg·m², and b is the total viscous friction in N·m·s/rad.'

where: Section 1 and exam traps, Kt–Kb equality
problem: 'Kt and Kb are often equal numerically when losses are ignored' is a hedge that can confuse. In SI with N·m/A and V·s/rad the two constants are equal by energy conservation; the loss caveat belongs to efficiency, not to the constant relation.
fix: Say: 'In SI units Kt (N·m/A) and Kb (V·s/rad) have the same numerical value, because mechanical power Kt·i·ω equals electrical power Kb·ω·i. Keep them as separate symbols, and always use the values the question gives.'

problem: The block notes give fixed numbers (Kt = 0.5 N·m/A, Kb = 0.5 V·s/rad) in a diagram meant to be general, so a reader may take them as fixed motor data rather than the worked-example values.
fix: Label the blocks with symbols only (Kt, Kb s), or add '(values from Worked example 1)' to the notes.
